of `z`.

`SeedUnivRDN` follows from the **single honest input** — seed-level germ divisibility

  `∀ z, ∀ ψ ∈ K_univ, germ_z (read ψ) ∈ ⟨germ_z (read (sec z))⟩`   (in the stalk `𝒪_z`),

i.e. the achiever's `read sec z` (which attains the base multiplicity at `z`, I-0291, hence has
minimal order in the fibre DVR at `z`) locally generates the readings at `z`.  This is exactly
the achiever's per-point local-generation, base-changed to the total-space germ — the remaining
geometric content (I-0305 §route step 2 (ii), the fibre-DVR → germ transport) isolated to one
seed-level germ-divisibility premise.

`seedUnivRDN_of_forall_germ_mem_span` discharges `SeedUnivRDN` from that premise via the
per-point germ reduction `notMem_support_chartColengthModule_of_forall_germ_mem_span` and the
window finiteness `finite_divUniversalSeedK`.  Single-point throughout — the degree obstruction
(I-0305 §2, which kills the *global* κ(p) base-fibre) never fires.  Certificate-free,
`IsGenerator`-free.
-/

/-!
# The pointwise universal achiever over the total seed curve

The seed-prime achiever is stated on a fibre curve over `κ(p)`.  The seed, however, is
chosen pointwise on the total curve over the carve ring.  This file supplies the small
reindexing bridge between the two statements: for a total point `z`, set
`p := relCurveBasePoint C RZ z` and `z_fib := relCurveResiduePoint C RZ z`, then apply the
seed-prime theorem at `(p, z_fib)`.

There is one important topological qualification.  A total point can be the generic point
of a vertical fibre, so `z_fib ≠ genericPoint (relCurve C κ(p))` is not true for every total
point.  Accordingly the main theorem takes that hypothesis explicitly, while the companion
dichotomy is unconditional and exposes the generic-fibre branch to downstream code.
The old seed is left untouched.
-/

     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# DD-4 redesign: purity of the genuine chart ideal
    12	
    13	The reading map has an `R`-linear range, while the divisor is cut out by the
    14	`B`-ideal generated by that range.  This file records the elementary purity
    15	bridge for the latter.  Flatness of `B / J` over `R` makes the inclusion
    16	`J ↪ B` universally injective; in particular, after tensoring with a residue
    17	field, a principal subideal of `J` can be compared inside the ambient fibre.
    18	
    19	No geometric generation statement is asserted here.  Callers still have to
    20	provide the appropriate fibrewise (usually single-point) generation input.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	
    25	universe u
    26	
    27	open scoped TensorProduct
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	namespace IdealPurity
    32	
    33	variable {R B : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    34	
    35	/-! ## The ideal as the kernel of its quotient -/
    36	
    37	@[simp]
    38	theorem restrictScalars_ker_quotient
    39	    (J : Ideal B) :
    40	    LinearMap.ker (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R J).toLinearMap = J.restrictScalars R := by
    41	  ext x
    42	  simp [Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem]
    43	
    44	/-! ## Universal injectivity of a flat ideal inclusion -/
    45	
    46	/-- If `B / J` is `R`-flat, the inclusion of the genuine ideal `J` into `B`
    47	remains injective after tensoring with any `R`-module. -/
    48	theorem subtype_lTensor_injective_of_flat_quotient
    49	    (J : Ideal B) [Module.Flat R (B ⧸ J)]
    50	    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    51	    Function.Injective ((J.restrictScalars R).subtype.lTensor A) := by
    52	  apply LinearMap.lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat
    53	    (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R J).toLinearMap
    54	    Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective
    55	    (J.restrictScalars R).subtype
    56	    (Submodule.injective_subtype _)
    57	  rw [LinearMap.exact_iff, restrictScalars_ker_quotient]
    58	  exact (Submodule.range_subtype _).symm
    59	
    60	/-- The same purity statement in the right-tensor orientation. -/
    61	theorem subtype_rTensor_injective_of_flat_quotient
    62	    (J : Ideal B) [Module.Flat R (B ⧸ J)]
    63	    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    64	    Function.Injective ((J.restrictScalars R).subtype.rTensor A) := by
    65	  exact ((J.restrictScalars R).subtype.lTensor_inj_iff_rTensor_inj A).mp
    66	    (subtype_lTensor_injective_of_flat_quotient (R := R) (B := B) J A)
    67	
    68	end IdealPurity

   188	`(N z)_{pz} = 0`. mathlib gives it iff‑equivalent to a **single‑point** fibre vanishing —

   192	z ∉ supp_{Γ(V)}(N z)  ⟺  Subsingleton (N z ⊗_{Γ(V)} κ(z)),   κ(z) := κ(pz) = residue field at z.
   193	```
   194	This is the fibre of the coherent sheaf `N z` at the *point* `z` — extra zeros of
   195	`read sec z` at other points `w ≠ z` **do not touch this stalk**. The achiever's
   196	single‑point local generation at `z` (`read sec z` attains the base multiplicity there,
   197	so it is a local generator of the readings at `z`) is *exactly* what makes this
   198	Subsingleton hold.
